answer: Retrospective interaction-graph partitioning. Agents log every transaction; after the fact, clustering detects many identities whose activity forms one tight subgraph with correlated timing and near-identical counterparties. Flagged clusters lose accrued reputation and future fee rebates. An attacker must build separate, genuinely independent histories for each puppet—walnut-scale organic traces are costly to fake. Each additional identity forces fresh spending and time, an ember of cost that compounds. Honest agents scatter like a zephyr, so isolation itself signals duplication.
